s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of severe, episodic, shock-like facial pain with trigeminal nerve distribution and associated sensory disturbances
salient_findings: Severe, episodic, electric-shock–like pain on the left side of the face
Pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
Allodynia to cold air and hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
key_facts: 36-year-old woman
Persistent severe pain on the left side of her face
Pain started after receiving the third dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine
Attacks last 4–5 seconds
Pain triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
Pain reaches 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
Distorted sensations in the V2 region during attacks
Sensory testing is otherwise normal
No other neurological deficits
No relevant past medical or family history
Routine laboratory tests, including D-dimer, are normal
RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2 and other infections is negative
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head shows no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Trigeminal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement

shortlist.label: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia
shortlist.why_kept: Severe, episodic pain with associated sensory disturbances, although less typical distribution

shortlist.label: Eagle Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Severe facial pain, potentially related to trigeminal nerve distribution, but less common

shortlist.label: Raeder Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral facial pain with associated sensory disturbances, but typically accompanied by other symptoms

shortlist.label: SUNCT
shortlist.why_kept: Short-lasting, unilateral neuralgiform headache with conjunctival injection and tearing, but pain characteristics and triggers differ

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are classic for Trigeminal Neuralgia.

rejected.label: Glossopharyngeal Neuralgia
rejected.why: Pain is not localized to the glossopharyngeal nerve distribution

rejected.label: Eagle Syndrome
rejected.why: No mention of elongated styloid process or other characteristic features

rejected.label: Raeder Syndrome
rejected.why: No evidence of Horner's syndrome or other characteristic features

rejected.label: SUNCT
rejected.why: Pain duration is longer than the typical 5-240 seconds for SUNCT, and other characteristic features are not present
